title: I Recorded the Overnight Construction After the Landlord Said It Was HVAC

parts.text: I woke at 1:19 a.m. to a saw that was not a furnace. The landlord had texted: HVAC maintenance, sorry for hum. This was not a hum. This was tile. I was thirty, standing in a T-shirt, holding my phone against the wall that smelled like new mastic. I recorded two minutes, then ten. In the morning the hallway had a pile of broken backsplash. The notice on the wall said emergency plumbing. I asked the workers. They said kitchen remodel for the unit the landlord's son was moving into. I mailed the recordings and the two contradictory notices to the housing inspector listed on my lease. Then the landlord slipped a note under my door: stop harassing contractors or I will non-renew.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He threatened non-renewal for recording a remodel he called HVAC.

social.video_title: The HVAC hum was a saw at 1:19 a.m. — Part 1/2
social.description: Mastic smell, two notices, and a son getting a kitchen. Then a threat under the door. Would you have kept recording?

parts.text: The inspector does not like overnight tile. Work hours snapped back to 8 to 5. The non-renewal note became a documented retaliation complaint. I stayed through the year because the lease said I could. The son got his kitchen in daylight. I slept. The wall stopped smelling like mastic at night. I keep the wav files. HVAC still hums, which is allowed. Saws have a union with the sun.

social.description: Retaliation note, legal hours, sleep. Was a son's kitchen an emergency?
